incidents-bot: :rotating_light: INCIDENT P2 — sudden spike in cache miss rate for prefix 'cli-emb-v2' on region-us-west-2. Alert threshold breached at 2026-03-15T09:12:01Z. Pager routed to @eve-oncall and @alice.sre. Logs auto-collected to /incidents/2187654321/logs

Eve-oncall: Acked. seeing 4x increase in prefix miss rate and 30% request latency tail lift. Putting initial mitigation: 1) enable fallback-model routing (cpu) 2) bump dedicated pool size +20% 3) set cache warm policy for affected prefixes. Will update in 10m. :thumbsup:

Alice.sre: Copy. I'm starting timeline build and grabbing logs. Need quick list of recent deploys touching tokenizer/model-serving or cache key code. @ben.eng @carla-ml can you confirm any push in last 6h?

Ben.eng: Pushed a small routing change ~3h ago (2026-03-15T06:05Z) that added a salt rotation flag to the cache key function, gated behind feature flag `salt-rotate-v2`. It was supposed to be off for prod, but I see the flag turned on for a subset of instances in us-west-2 during the deploy. Investigating rollout state.

Carla-ml: We rolled model version cli-emb-v2@2.3.4 at 02:30Z — that model uses tokenizer update token-prepend behavior (adds '\u0002' prefix) compared to 2.3.3. If cache key doesn't normalize tokens, that could split prefix keys.

Alice.sre: Good catch. Possible hypotheses: H1) token-prefix change in model caused cache key mismatch (different canonicalization) H2) salt-rotate flag partial rollout caused inconsistent key hashing across hosts H3) eviction storm due to TTL misalignment after recent config change.

Grace-support: Customer impact: seeing increased error rates and slowdowns for ~7 customers (mid-market). Top 3 impacted: AcmeApps (50% requests degraded), NimbusPay (20%), EduForge (10%). No SLO breaches yet but paging thresholds hit. I've opened tickets and letting CS know.

Eve-oncall: Live mitigation update: rolled back feature flag `salt-rotate-v2` on the subset, scaled pool +25%, and enabled aggressive warm for cli-emb-v2 prefixes. Early indicators: miss-rate fell from 72% to 46% in 6m. Latency tail improving.

Frank-ops: Sharing quick queries — run these on log-warehouse: 
```
-- prefix miss counts by host
SELECT host, count(*) AS misses
FROM cache.events
WHERE prefix = 'cli-emb-v2' AND ts > now() - interval '1 hour'
GROUP BY host
ORDER BY misses DESC
LIMIT 50;
```
and 
```
-- key fingerprint diff
SELECT key_hash, count(*) FROM cache.keys
WHERE ts BETWEEN now()-interval '6 hours' AND now()
GROUP BY key_hash ORDER BY count DESC LIMIT 100;
```
Posting results link: https://logs.internal/redwood/2187654321/results

Ben.eng: From host-level logs I see a mixing of two key formats: `k:v1:sha256(...)` and `k:v2:sha256(salt+...)`. The `salt-rotate-v2` flag toggles the latter. That explains inconsistent hits across hosts.

Carla-ml: Token prepending also changes the 'prefix' strings used for caching. When combined with salt change you get a combinatorial missset. Looks like H1+H2 combined.

Alice.sre: Timeline so far: 02:30Z model rollout (cli-emb-v2@2.3.4) -> 06:05Z routing deploy with feature flag -> 06:15Z partial flag flip in us-west-2 -> 09:12Z alert. Need to sync with deploy logs to confirm exact flag flip time.

Eve-oncall: I'm doing an on-call handoff in ~1h. @alice.sre can you prepare a short summary and open a follow-up RCA thread? I'll hand off to @frank-ops in 55m.

Alice.sre: Will do. Adding immediate action items in-thread: 
- item: confirm and revert any unintended flag flips (done for subset, still verifying) 
- item: invalidate legacy keys quickly for cli-emb-v2 to force warm (run invalidation job) 
- item: coordinate consistent key format rollout (either normalize keys or do full rollout) 
- item: gather correlated traces for impacted customers (AcmeApps/NimbusPay/EduForge)

Frank-ops: I've kicked an invalidation job targeting `cli-emb-v2:*` prefixes with a small concurrency cap. Monitor for downstream load spike.

Grace-support: Noted. Raising customer comms draft: short blurb + ETA for mitigation. Will wait for final confirmation before sending to customers.

Ben.eng: Proposed long-term fix: add deterministic normalization layer in cache-key pipeline that strips tokenizer-internal prefix tokens and makes salt rotation explicit in the key namespace (e.g., `k:canonical:v<saltver>:hash`). Short-term: full rollback of `salt-rotate-v2` and coordinated model/tokenizer rollout.

Alice.sre: Hypotheses status: H1 (token change) = likely; H2 (partial salt rollout) = confirmed contributor; H3 (TTL eviction) = low evidence so far. Marking H1/H2 as primary root cause pending final logs.

Eve-oncall: Quick status 30m after mitigations: miss-rate at 24% (was 72%), latency p99 reduced by 230ms, customer impact reduced to minor. Keeping oncall for 1h to watch.

Carla-ml: I'll schedule a rollback of tokenizer behavior to older canonicalization if we can't ship normalization quick. Also will add unit tests for cache-key invariants.

Alice.sre: Collecting artifacts for RCA: links -> deploy logs: https://deploys.internal/commit/sha12345, flag audit: https://flags.internal/audit/2187654321, logs bundle: https://logs.internal/redwood/2187654321/bundle.tar.gz

Eve-oncall: Handoff note for @frank-ops: all mitigations applied, primary root cause pointer = combined tokenizer + partial salt rollout. Watch for resurgence after invalidation job completes. Customer comms draft waiting.

Frank-ops: Taking over monitoring. I'll post a concise follow-up timeline and assign the RCA write-up.

Grace-support: After final confirmation please ping me and I'll push the customer update. Also request SLO exception if needed.

Alice.sre: Final note in-thread: TL;DR: incident caused by mismatch in cache key formats due to an inadvertent partial feature-flag rollout plus tokenizer change in new model. Immediate mitigations (flag rollback, invalidation, pool scale, warm) reduced impact. Next steps: RCA doc, permanent normalization fix, rollout playbook update.

incidents-bot: Incident transitioned to 'mitigated' at 2026-03-15T10:03:07Z. Follow-up RCA assigned to eng-sre and eng teams. :white_check_mark:
